package_info.why_malicious: N/A – This report does not analyze a specific malicious package. Instead, it highlights the security risks associated with the absence of Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) in software supply chains, emphasizing that lack of SBOMs impedes risk management, vulnerability tracking, and detection of malicious or outdated dependencies.

behavioral_signatures: Software vendors do not provide SBOMs during procurement or updates, preventing visibility into software components.
Organizations lack an up-to-date inventory of internal and third-party software assets, including open-source dependencies.
No process exists for tracking or verifying the provenance and integrity of third-party and open-source components within deployed software.
file_indicators: Absence of SBOM documentation files (e.g., missing CycloneDX, SPDX, or similar SBOM formats) in software deliverables.
No inventory or manifest files listing dependencies or internal software assets within the software package or deployment artifacts.
network_indicators: N/A – The report does not describe any network-based indicators or malicious network activity.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: To detect supply chain risks related to missing SBOMs, organizations should require SBOM documentation from all software vendors and verify its presence and completeness using automated tools. Scanners can check for standard SBOM formats (e.g., CycloneDX, SPDX) and cross-reference declared dependencies with actual software components. Any absence of SBOMs, incomplete dependency manifests, or discrepancies between declared and observed components should be flagged for further investigation as potential supply chain security risks.
